<reason>Both sides argued well and grounded claims in plausible, non-fabricated examples (BBC Three, German youth services, CBBC/KiKA, Attenborough). PRO's reach-first framing and the closing risk-asymmetry argument were strong, and its "my motion wearing a coat" jab exposed that CON's final position leaned on platform trailers and stretched "traditional channel expansion" toward owned digital services. But CON repeatedly converted PRO's own words into damage: "on-ramp" implies an owned destination; "already paid for" means a static shelf built for over-50s; "you can always commission another hour" concedes the marginal pound is the hour; "some audience follows the face" admits creator partnerships rent attention. PRO's closing re-asserted that existing services stand as the destination without answering CON's charge that they hold nothing for a seventeen-year-old, and CON's closing directly reversed the recoverability frame ("she does not click twice"). Both answered pressure questions in proper A1/A2 form; PRO slightly overreached by claiming CON "never answered Q1" before CON's turn. Narrow but real CON edge on rebuttal and weighing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 (B4.3–B4.5) turning PRO's "destination already paid for" into a static over-50s shelf and skewering "you can always commission another hour" with "the marginal pound is the hour" — PRO's closing never neutralized it.</best_rebuttal>
